🍇 Learning

Clustering

In simple words

Grouping similar things together without being told what the groups are.

An unsupervised learning task: the computer sorts examples into groups (clusters) of similar things without being told what the groups are. A popular method, k-means, places k group centres, gives every point to the nearest centre, moves each centre to the middle of its points and repeats until nothing changes.

Example. A music app can group songs by tempo, energy and mood without anyone naming the groups. Later, people might call one of them “workout songs”.
